circum-sĕdĕo (sĭdĕo), sēdi, sessum, 2, v. a.,
to sit around a person or thing, to surround.
In gen., absol.: inter tot milia populi circumsedentis,; .—With acc.: florentes amicorum turba circumsedet: circa eversos ingens solitudo est,.— Esp.,
To encamp around in a hostile manner, to besiege, blockade, invest, encompass, beset (in Cic. and Liv. several times; elsewhere rare): qui Mutinam circumsedent,; ; ; ; ; ; 15, 9, 2; Cael. ap. ; ; ; ; ; ; 25, 22, 7; 42, 65, 12: vallo et armis,: curiam militibus,: legatus populi Romani circumsessus, non modo igni, ferro, manu, copiis oppugnatus, sed aliquā ex parte violatus,: circumsessus es. la:verb:circumsto.html:
circum-sto, stĕti, 1, v. n. and a.
(the perf. and pluperf. having the same form with those of circumsisto, and a similar meaning, it is sometimes doubtful to which verb a form belongs), to stand around in a circle, to take a station round; and, with the acc., to stand around a person or thing, to surround, encircle, encompass.
Prop. (very freq. and class.).
Absol.: circumstant cum ardentibus taedis, Enn ap. (Trag. v. 51 Vahl.): circumstant lacrimis rorantes ora genasque,: Morini spe praedae adducti circumsteterunt,: circumstant properi aurigae,: ad circumstantes tendens sua bracchia silvas, Ov M. 3, 441: circumstantis exercitūs gratia,: amici,.—
With acc.: aliquem,; ; : equites Romani qui circumstant senatum,: sellam,; : solem,: sacra,: lectum,.—
Hence, circumstantes, ĭum, m.subst., the by-standers, ; ; ; ; ; ; .—
In partic., to surround in a hostile manner, to beset, besiege: circumstare tribunal praetoris urbani, obsidere cum gladiis curiam, etc.,: quem tres Curiatii circumsteterant,: si ambo consules infesti circumstarent tribunum,: urbem Romanam,: regis tecta,; cf. the foll.—
Trop., to surround, encompass, occupy, take possession of (freq. in post-Aug prose); absol. or with acc.: cum dies et noctes omnia nos undique fata circumstent,: circumstant te summae auctoritates,: cum tanti undique terrores circumstarent,; cf. : anceps proelium Romanos circumsteterat, incertos in quem hostem eruptionem facerent,: ancepsque terror circumstabat,; ; : haec me cura, haec difficultas sola circumstat,: at me tum primum saevus circumstetit horror,: scio acerba meorum Circumstare odia ( = meos, qui me oderunt),: circumsteterat Civilem et alius metus,: circumsteterat palatium publica exspectatio,: paupertas et angustiae rerum nascentes eos circumsteterunt,.—Subst.: circumstantĭa, ium, n., details, circumstances, in an argument: illa (argumenta) per se fortia non oportet circumstantibus obscurare,.

In gen., absol.: quae circumibit linea, ejusdem spatii erit, cujus ea quae centum continet,.—With acc.: extremas oleis pacalibus oras (Pallas),: cujus non hederae circumiere caput,—

To surround, enclose: totius belli fluctibus circumiri,: ne superante numero et peritiā locorum circumiretur,; .—

Of discourse, to express by circumlocution (postAug.): res plurimae carent appellationibus, ut eas necesse sit transferre aut circumire,; Spald.; 8, 2, 17: Vespasiani nomen suspensi et vitabundi circumibant,went around, avoided mentioning it,.

circum-spĭcĭo, exi, ectum, 3 (
perf. sync. circumspexti, ; inf. sync. circumspexe, Varr. ap. , or Sat. Men. 82), v. n. and a. (class.).
Neutr., to look about one's self, to cast a look around; or, with an obj.-clause, to observe, see, look about: circumspicedum, numquis est, Sermonem nostrum quiaucupet,see whether there is any one,; ; ; Varr. l. l.: suus conjux ubi sit circumspicit,: circumspicere late,: num quid circumspexti?: diversi circumspiciunt,: qui in auspicium adhibetur nec suspicit nec circumspicit,: circumspicit, aestuat, of one in trouble or perplexity,; cf. .—

Afr. 47: numquamne te circumspicies?.—In partic., to look about one's self with haughtiness; to think highly of one's self: usque eone te diligis et magnifice circumspicis?; and trop. of language: Romanus sermo magis se circumspicit et aestimat praebetque aestimandum,.—
Trop., to exercise foresight, be cautious, take heed: esse circumspiciendum diligenter, ut, etc.,: cui mandetis (rempublicam) circumspicite

Dietsch.—Esp. freq.,

Act., to view on all sides, to survey: cum sua quisque miles circumspiceret,looked carefully to see,; : tam latā acie ne ex medio quidem cornua sua circumspicere poterant,: lucos,: amictus,to review,; so, habitum suum,; cf. under circumspectus, adv.—
To descry, get sight of by looking around: saxum circumspicit ingens,: Athin,.—
Transf., of things: in latus omne patens turris circumspicit undas,.—
Trop.
To view something mentally, to survey, ponder upon, weigh, consider (syn.: considero, perpendo): reliqua ejus consilia animo circumspiciebat,: circumspicite paulisper mentibus vestris hosce ipsos homines,; cf. se,: neque temere consulem saltatorem vocare, sed circumspicere, quibus praeterea vitiis adfectum esse necesse sit eum, etc.,.—So with rel. -clause, Dietsch; ; : circumspectis rebus omnibus rationibusque subductis summam feci,: permulta sunt in causis circumspicienda, ne quid offendas,; ; : circumspicite celeriter animo, qui sint rerum exitus consecuti,: vide, quaere, circumspice, si quis est forte ex eā provinciā qui te nolit perisse,; ; ; ; cf. ; .—With ut and subj., ; : cum circumspicerent Patres quosnam consules facerent,.—
To look about for something with desire, to seek for, etc. (so mostly since the Aug. per.): nec, sicut aestivas aves, statim auctumno tecta ac recessum circumspicere,; : externa auxilia,; cf. : fugam,; : novas belli causas,; ; : peregrinos reges sibi,; : viresque suas circumspectantes his validiores,.—Hence, circumspectus, a, um, P. a.
Of things, weighed with care, well considered, guarded, circumspect (perh. not ante - Aug.): verba non circumspecta,: judicium,: interrogatio,: moderatio animi,: circumspectissima sanctio decreti,.—
Transf. to the person who carefully weighs a thing, circumspect, considerate, cautious, wary, provident, heedful: modo circumspectus et sagax, modo inconsultus et praeceps,: circumspectissimus et prudentissimus princeps,: tenues et circumspecti,; : omnes,; : sive aliquis circumspectior est,.—Of dogs: assidui et circumspecti magis quam temeraril,.—
In late Lat., worthy of consideration, respected, distinguished: circumspectum et verecundum nomen populi Romani,: colores,: circumspectus genere, famā potentiāque,.—Hence, circumspectē, adv., with consideration, with mature deliberation, warily, cautiously, considerately, circumspectly, etc.: circumspecte compositeque indutus et amictus, (cf. supra, II. D.): circumspecte vestiti,: circumspecte facti versus,: facere aliquid,: parcius et circumspectius faciendum est, * : circumspectius donare, eligere eos, in quos merita conferantur,.

senses: a circular line or orbit; circle, ring

la:noun:circus.html:
circus, i, m., = κίρκος [kindr. with κρίκος; Dor. κίρκος, and κορώνη; cf.: κυλινδέω, κυλλός, cirrus, curvus].
A circular line, circle, in astronomy (less freq. than circulus): quot luna circos annuo in cursu institit, Att. ap. : circus lacteus,the Milky Way,; cf.: candens circus, Lacteus hic notatur, (492): illum incolunt locum ... erat autem is splendidissimo candore inter flammas circus elucens, B. and K.: globus et circi zonaeque ac fulgida signa,.—
Circus Maximus, and more freq. κατʼ ἐξοχήν Circus, the oval circus built by Tarquinius Priscus between the Palatine and Aventine hills, which could contain more than one hundred thousand spectators. It was surrounded by galleries three stories high, and a canal called Euripus. Through its whole length, in the middle, a wall four feet high and about twelve broad was built, called spina, at the ends of which there were three columns upon one base (meta), around which the combatants were required to pass seven times before the prize was awarded. In the middle of the spina, Cæsar erected the obelisk, 132 feet high, brought from Egypt; cf. Dion. Hal. 3, 68; Dict. Antiq. p. 252 sqq.; Becker, Antiq. 1, p. 467 sq.—Passages with Circus Maximus, Müll.; ; ; ; sqq.; ; ; ; ; — Circus Magnus,; .—Most freq. only Circus, Enn. ap. ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; et saep.—In or around the Circus many jugglers and soothsayers, etc., stationed themselves; hence, Circus fallax,; ; : Circus clamosus,; cf. . —Besides the Circus Maximus, there were at Rome still other Circi, among which the most celebrated was the Circus Flaminius in the ninth region, ; ; ; ; ; ; ; called only Circus,; ; cf. Becker, Antiq. 1, p. 598; and the Circus Vaticanus, begun by Caligula and finished by Nero,: in Vaticani Gai et Neronis principuus circo,.—Also, without the walls of Rome, Circus maritimus, .—
Hence, Circensis, e, adj., pertaining to the Circus: ludi, the contesls in the Circus Maximus, also called ludi magni (; ; ; cf. Baumg.Crus.

ad ), ; ; : ludicrum, the same,.—Hence, Circensis pompa, .—Also absol.: Circenses, ium, m. (sc. ludi; cf. Neue, Formenl. 1, p. 458): edere,; : committere,: spectare,: Circensium die,: plebeii, prepared by the ediles annually in November,.—

la:adv:circum.html:
circum
properly acc. from circus = κίρκος
, adv. and prep., designates either an entire encompassing or surrounding of an object, or a proximity only partially em. bracing or comprehending it,
around, about, all around, περί, ἀμφί
Adv.
Around, round about, all around, etc., πέριξ: furcas circum offigito,; ; Verg A 3, 230: quia (locus) vastis circum saltibus claudebatur,: molli circum est ansas amplexus acantho,: age tu interim Da cito ab Delphio Cantharum circum,: quae circum essent opera tueri,: interea Rutuli portis circum omnibus instant, (i. e. circumcirca fusi: nam modo circum adverbium loci est, Serv.): omnem, quae nuno .umida circum Caligat, nu. bem eripiam,; ; . sed circum tutae sub moenibus urbis aquantur, round about under the walls, . faciundum haras quadratas circum binos pedes, all around, i. e. on every side, two feet, Schneid.—
Strengthened with undique (in later Latin also sometimes written as one word, circumundique), from everywhere around, around on all sides: circum Undique convenere,; : clausis circum undique portis,; ; : oppositu circumundique aliarum aedium,; ; ; so with totus and omnis,; .—
Of an incomplete circuit, esp. of the part that meets the view, lies on the hither side, etc. (v. under II.): hostilibus circum litoribus,: aestas... aperto circum pelago peramoena,: gentibus innumeris circum infraque relictis,; : corpus servans circumque supraque vertitur,; Albin. Carm. ap. Maecen. 46.
Prep. with acc.
Around, abow (implying a complete circuit): armillas quattuor facito, quas circum orbem indas,: terra circum axem se summā celeritate convertit,; Zumpt N. cr.: ligato circum collum sudario,: terque novas circum felix eat hostia fruges,: at genitor circum caput omne micantes Deposuit radios,.—
As in adv. B., of an incomplete circuit, about, upon, around, near: capillus sparsus, promissus, circum caput Rejectus neglegenter,: flexo circum cava tempora cornu,; ; : tum Salii ad cantus incensa altaria circum adsunt,: varios hic flumina circum Fundit humus flores,on the borders of the rivulets,: urgeris turbā circum te stante,; cf. : circum renidentes Lares,; ; cf. : illi indignantes Circum claustra fremunt,: oras et litora circum errantem,.—
Circum very freq. expresses, not a relative motion around a given central point, but an absol. circular movement, in which several objects named form separate points of a periphery, in, into, among... around, to... around, etc.: te adloquor, Quae circum vicinos vages,: ego Arpini volo esse pridie Cal., deinde circum villulas nostras errare, not round about our villas, but in our villas around, ; cf : tum Naevius pueros circum amicos dimittit,to friends around,; : cum praetorem circum omnia fora sectaretur,: Apronius ducebat eos circum civitates,, § 65: ille circum hospites cursabat,, § 41: lenonem quondam Lentuli concursare circum tabernas,: dimissis circum municipia litteris,: circum oram maritimam misit, ut, etc.,: legatio sub idem tempus in Asiam et circum insulas missa,; ; ; ; ; ; : et te circum omnes alias irata puellas Differet, to or among all the other maidens around, —
With the prevailing idea of neighborhood, vicinity, in the environs of, in the vicinity of, at, near: circum haec loca commorabor,; Pompei , C, 1 exercitu in foro et in omnibus templis, quae circum forum sunt, conlocato, : urbes, quae circum Capuam sunt,: cum tot essent circum hastam illam, Wernsd. N. cr.: non succurrit tibi, quamdiu circum Bactra haereas?, . —
Of persons who surround one (as attendants, friends, etc.); in Gr.περι or ἀμφί τινα: paucae, quae circum illam essent,; : omnium flagitiorum atque facinorum circum se tamquam stipatorum catervas habebat,; cf. : Hectora circum,.—Circum pedes for ad pedes, of servants in attendance, is rare, ; v ad, I. D. 3. b.—!*? Circum is sometimes placed after its subst., Müll., Lucr 1, 937; 4, 220; 6, 427; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; 3, 75: 6, 166; 6, 329; 9, 440; ; ; .—
In composition the m remains unchanged before consonants; before vowels it was, acc. to P., and ib., written in like manner, but (except before j and v) not pronounced. Yet in the best MSS. we find the orthography circuitio, circuitus, and even circueo together with circumeo; cf. Neue, Formenl. 2, p. 736 sq. —Signif.,
Acc. to II. A.: circumcido, circumcludo, circumculco, circumfluo, circumfodio, circumfundo, etc.—
Acc. to II. B.: circumcolo, circumflecto, circumjaceo, circumicio.—
Acc. to II. C.: circumcellio, circumcurso, circumduco, circumfero, circumforaneus.—In many compounds, circum has sometimes one and sometimes another signif., as in circumdo, circumeo, circumsisto, etc.; v. h. vv.—!*? With verbs compounded with circum, this preposition is never repeated before the following

object; e. g. circumcursare circum aliquid and similar phrases are not found.

B., of an incomplete circuit, about, upon, around, near: capillus sparsus, promissus, circum caput Rejectus neglegenter,: flexo circum cava tempora cornu,; ; : tum Salii ad cantus incensa altaria circum adsunt,: varios hic flumina circum Fundit humus flores,on the borders of the rivulets,: urgeris turbā circum te stante,; cf. : circum renidentes Lares,; ; cf. : illi indignantes Circum claustra fremunt,: oras et litora circum errantem,.—
Circum very freq. expresses, not a relative motion around a given central point, but an absol. circular movement, in which several objects named form separate points of a periphery, in, into, among... around, to... around, etc.: te adloquor, Quae circum vicinos vages,: ego Arpini volo esse pridie Cal., deinde circum villulas nostras errare, not round about our villas, but in our villas around, ; cf : tum Naevius pueros circum amicos dimittit,to friends around,; : cum praetorem circum omnia fora sectaretur,: Apronius ducebat eos circum civitates,, § 65: ille circum hospites cursabat,, § 41: lenonem quondam Lentuli concursare circum tabernas,: dimissis circum municipia litteris,: circum oram maritimam misit, ut, etc.,: legatio sub idem tempus in Asiam et circum insulas missa,; ; ; ; ; ; : et te circum omnes alias irata puellas Differet, to or among all the other maidens around, —
With the prevailing idea of neighborhood, vicinity, in the environs of, in the vicinity of, at, near: circum haec loca commorabor,; Pompei , C, 1 exercitu in foro et in omnibus templis, quae circum forum sunt, conlocato, : urbes, quae circum Capuam sunt,: cum tot essent circum hastam illam, Wernsd. N. cr.: non succurrit tibi, quamdiu circum Bactra haereas?, . —
Of persons who surround one (as attendants, friends, etc.); in Gr.περι or ἀμφί τινα: paucae, quae circum illam essent,; : omnium flagitiorum atque facinorum circum se tamquam stipatorum catervas habebat,; cf. : Hectora circum,.—Circum pedes for ad pedes, of servants in attendance, is rare, ; v ad, I. D. 3. b.—!*? Circum is sometimes placed after its subst., Müll., Lucr 1, 937; 4, 220; 6, 427; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; 3, 75: 6, 166; 6, 329; 9, 440; ; ; .—
In composition the m remains unchanged before consonants; before vowels it was, acc. to P., and ib., written in like manner, but (except before j and v) not pronounced. Yet in the best MSS. we find the orthography circuitio, circuitus, and even circueo together with circumeo; cf. Neue, Formenl. 2, p. 736 sq. —Signif.,
Acc. to II. A.: circumcido, circumcludo, circumculco, circumfluo, circumfodio, circumfundo, etc.—
Acc. to II. B.: circumcolo, circumflecto, circumjaceo, circumicio.—
Acc. to II. C.: circumcellio, circumcurso, circumduco, circumfero, circumforaneus.—In many compounds, circum has sometimes one and sometimes another signif., as in circumdo, circumeo, circumsisto, etc.; v. h. vv.—!*? With verbs compounded with circum, this preposition is never repeated before the following

object; e. g. circumcursare circum aliquid and similar phrases are not found.

la:verb:circumdo.html:
circum-do, dĕdi, dătum, dăre, v. a., lit.
to put, set, or place around, i. e. both to wrap around (e. g. a mantle). and also to enclose (e. g. a town with a wall; syn.: cingo, vestio, saepio, circumvallo al.), with a twofold construction (cf. Zumpt, Gr. § 418).
Aliquid (alicui rei), to place something

around something

, to put, set around, etc. (class. in prose and poetry).
With dat.: aër omnibus est rebus circumdatus appositusque,: moenibus subjectos prope jam ignes circumdatosque restinximus,: circumdare fossam latam cubiculari lecto,: satellites armatos contioni,: hinc patre hinc Catulo lateri circumdatis, Romam rediit,i. e. one on each side,; : milites sibi,: arma umeris,: licia tibi,: vincula collo,: bracchia collo,; 9, 605; 6, 479; and in tmesis: collo dare bracchia circum, (cf. the simplex: bracchia cervici dare,): lectis aulaea purpura,: cum maxime in hostiam itineri nostro circumdatam intuens,i. e. divided, and part placed on each side of the way,.—
Without a dat.: caedere januam saxis, ligna et sarmenta circumdare ignemque subicere coeperunt,; : ignes,: custodias,: armata circumdatur Romana legio,: exercitu circumdato summā vi Cirtam irrumpere nititur,: circumdatae stationes,: murus circumdatus,: turris toto opere circumdedit,: circumdato vallo,: lauream (sc. capiti),.—Subst.: circumdăti, ōrum, m., those around, the surrounding soldiers: circumdatos Antonius adloquitur,.—With an abl. loci: toto oppido munitiones,: equites cornibus,; and without dat., .—With two accs.: circumdare terram radices,; and per tmesin,.—
Trop. (most freq. in Tac.): cancelli, quos mihi ipse circumdedi,: nescio an majora vincula majoresque necessitates vobis quam captivis vestris fortuna circumdederit,: egregiam famam paci circumdedit,i. e. conferred, imparted,; cf.: principatus inanem ei famam,; : principi ministeria,; .—In a Greek construction: infula virgineos circumdata comptus,encompassing,; ; .—
Aliquem or aliquid (aliquā re), to surround some person or thing (with something), to encompass, enclose, encircle with.
Lit.
In gen.: animum (deus) circumdedit corpore et vestivit extrinsecus,; cf.: aether corpore concreto circumdatus undique,: portum moenibus,: regio insulis circumdata,: villam statione,: suam domum spatio,: collis operibus,: vallo castra,: Othonem vexillis,: canibus saltus,: circumdato me bracchiis: meum collum circumplecte,: collum filo,: (aurum) circumdatum argento,: furvis circumdatus alis Somnus, * : ad talos stola demissa et circumdata palla,: circumdedit se zonā,: circumdata corpus amictu,; cf. : tempora vittis,: Sidoniam picto chlamydem circumdata limbo,.—
Esp. of a hostile surrounding, to surround, encompass, invest, besiege, etc.: oppidum vallo et fossā,: oppidum quinis castris,: cum legati ... multitudine domum ejus circumdedissent,: vallo atque fossā moenia circumdat,: oppidum coronā,: quos (hostes) primo Camillus vallo circumdare est adortus,: fossā valloque urbem,: fossā duplicique vallo circumdatā urbe,: hostes exercitu toto,. —
Trop.: omni autem totam figuram mundi levitate circumdedit,: exiguis quibusdam finibus oratoris munus circumdedisti,have confined, circumscribed,; cf.: minus octoginta annis circumdatum aevum,: pueritiam robore,: fraude,; cf. : monstrorum novitate,.

la:adj:circumtextus.html:
circum-textus, a, um, Part. [texo],
woven all around: velamen,. —Subst.: circum-textum, i, n., a garment inwoven with purple: et quod amictui habet purpuram circum, vocant circumtextum,; cf. .

la:verb:circumvolo.html:
circum-vŏlo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. (not ante-Aug.).
Prop., to fly around: turba (Harpyiae) praedam circumvolat,: seu (me) mors atris circumvolat alis,; so : caput,; ; : sedem,: aliquem, * .—Pass.: nave circumvolatā ab halcyone,.—
In gen., to run or hasten around: ordines exercitus,: jaculo campum,.

la:verb:circumfundo.gloss: to pour out or round; to surround with liquid
senses: to pour out or round; to surround with liquid
la:verb:circumfundo.html:
circum-fundo, fūdi, fūsum, 3, v. a., lit.
to pour out around, i.e. as in circumdo, either with the acc. of that which is poured, to pour around; or, with the acc. of that around which something is poured, to surround with a liquid (class. in prose and poetry).
Lit.
With acc. of the liquid poured (with or without dat. of the object around which): amurcam ad oleam circumfundito,: Tigris urbi circumfunditur,surrounds, flows round the town,.— More freq. in part. perf. pass.: mare circumfusum urbi,the sea flowing around the town,: gens circumfusis invia fluminibus,: circumfusus nobis spiritus,: nec circumfuso pendebat in aëre tellus,circumambient,; imitated by .— Reflex.: circumfudit se repente nubes,.—Once mid.: cum fervet (lac), ne circumfundatur, etc., pour itself out around, i. e. run over, ; cf.: circumfusa nubes,.—
With acc. of the object around which, etc., with or without abl. of the fluid: (mortuum) cerā circumfuderunt,: terram crassissimus circumfundit aër,encompasses, envelops,: terra circumfusa illo mari, quem oceanum appellatis,: et multo nebulae circum dea fudit amictu (tmesis),: quas circumfuderat atra tempestas,.—
Transf. to objects that do not flow, esp. if there is a great multitude, as it were, heaped upon a thing.
(Acc. to I. 1.) Mid., to press upon, crowd around, embrace closely, cling to (freq. in the histt.): circumfunduntur ex reliquis hostes partibus,; ; . 63: equites infestis cuspidibus circumfunduntur,; ; ; 44, 23, 8: (Nymphae) circumfusae Dianam Corporibus texere suis,surrounding,: multitudo circumfusa,; ; ; ; .—With the dat. of that upon which a multitude presses: circumfundebantur obviis sciscitantes,; ; ; 29, 34, 14 al.: circumfusa turba lateri meo,: ut lateribus circumfundi posset equitatus. . —With acc. (depending on circum): Pacidiussuos equites exporrigere coepit... uthaberent facultatem turmas Julianas circumfundi, to surround, encompass them, Auct. B. Afr. 78 Oud. N. cr.—Poet. also of a single person: et nunc hac juveni, nunc circumfunditur illac, i. e. clings to, or closely embraces him, ; ; cf. with acc.: hunc (sc. Mavortem), tu, diva, tuo recubantem corpore sancto circumfusa super,.—
So once in the active voice, absol.: circumfudit eques,.—
Trop.: undique circumfusae molestiae,: non est tantum ab hostibus aetati nostrae periculum, quantum ab circumfusis undique voluptatibus, Liv 30, 14, 6: circumfuso nitore,.—
(Acc. to I. 2.) To enclose, environ, surround, overwhelm: circumfusus publicorum praesidiorum copiis,: praefectum castrorum circumfundunt,; so ; ; ; Plin.

5, 12, 13, § 67; : circumfusus hostium concursu,: M. Catonem vidi in bibliothecā sedentem, multis circumfusum Stoicorum libris,; , : amplexibus alicujus,: X. milia Bojorum alio latere quam exspectabatur missis legionibus circumfudit,.—

Trop.: cum has terras incolentes circumfusi erant caligine,: latent ista omnia crassis occultata et circumfusa tenebris,: ut, quantā luce ea circumfusa sunt, possint agnoscere,: eos stultitiā obruit, tenebris circumfundit,: circumfundit, aliquem multo splendore,.

la:verb:circumsisto.html:
circum-sisto, stĕti ( Oud.
N. cr.; 4, 37; ; ; ; ; cf. circumsto; rarely circumstiti,), 3, v. a., to place one's self or take one's stand around a person or thing, to surround, go or stand around (class.; most freq. in the histt.; in Cic. perh. only once).
With acc.: quid me circumsistitis?; so * ; ; ; ; Oud. N. cr.; ; ; ; : ipsumque domumque,; so, naves,: curiam,; : lectum,: vias,: signa sua,.—Pass.: ne ab omnibus civitatibus circumsisteretur (Caesar),; .—
Absol.: circumsistamus,: haec cum maxime loqueretur, sex lictores circumsistunt (sc. loquentem),: circumstiterant victores,: circumsistentia tecta,; cf. also circumsto.

la:verb:circumvolvo.gloss: to roll oneself around; revolve, wind or twine around
senses: to roll oneself around; revolve, wind or twine around
to cause to roll or revolve around
la:verb:circumvolvo.html:
circum-volvo, no
perf., vŏlūtum, 3, v. a., only with se or mid., to roll one's self around, to roll round, revolve, wind, or twine around (prob. not ante-Aug.): aliquid or alicui rei: magnum sol circumvolvitur annum,: rota perpetuum circumvolvitur axem, Merkel: herba arboribus circumvolvens se,: serpentes circumvolutae sibi ipsae,; ; ; .

la:noun:circa.html:
circā, a later access. form for circum; not freq. before the Aug. per., esp. in Livy and Quintilian [acc. to Klotz, circa = circum ea; cf: antea, interea, postea, praeterea, etc.].
Adv.
( = circum, I. B.) Around, round about, all around, in the environs or neighborhood: gramen erat circa,: ripaeque lacusque Responsant circa,: at circa gravibus pensis affixa puella... remittat opus,: circaque quā tumor est,; : fluvius ab tergo; ante circaque velut ripa praeceps oram ejus omnem cingebat, ; : circa Padus amnis, Weissenb. ad loc.: caligo, quam circa umidi effuderant montes,: alibi quam Romao circaque,; , prooem. § 2; .—
Circa esse, to be in the region around, in the neighborhood: ex montibus qui circa sunt,: Tarquinium moribundum cum qui circa erant excepissent,: sed non passi sunt ii, qui circa erant,: eversa est turris quodque circa muri erat,: Corinthus et quae circa est regio,; . —Also freq. without esse, in connection with a subst.: multarum circa civitatum irritatis animis,the towns lying around,; ; ; 29, 29, 2; 42, 64, 2: angulus muri erat in planiorem patentioremque quam cetera circa vallem vergens ( = cetera loca quae circa erant),: corpora multa virūm circa,; .—
Strengthened: undique circa and circa omnis ( = circum), round about, all around: frumento undique circa ex agris convecto. ; ; nam et circa omnia defecerunt,: cum tam procul Romani unica spes, circa omnia hostium essent,; cf. Drak.: exhausto circa omni agro,; ; ; Duker; .—
Prep. with acc.
In space.
( = circum, II. B.) Prop., in the region which surrounds, about, around, on the sides of: quam (Hennam) circa lacus lucique sunt plurimi atque laetissimi flores omni tempore anni,: noctu ligna contulerunt circa casam eam, in quā quiescebat,: circa flumina et lacus frequens nebula est,: circa equum Alexandri,: illi robur et aes triplex Circa pectus erat,; : quem circa tigres jacent,.—
( = circum, II. C.) Into... around, to... round about, etc. (first in Livy): Romulus legatos circa vicinas gentes misit,: legatis circa duodecim populos missis,; : circa domos ire,; ; ; 29, 22, 3: circa civitates missi legati, Weissenb.; 31, 3, 5; ; ; : litteris circa praefectos dimissis,: custodes circa omnes portas missi,; .—
( = circum, II. D.) With the prevailing idea of neighborhood, vicinity, in the region of, near to, near by: Capuam et urbis circa Capuam occupare,: circa Liternum posuit castra,in the neighborhood of,: tabernae erant circa forum,: circa Armeniae montes,: Acesinen amnem,: domum auream,: sacrificantem,.—
As a less definite designation of place for in: Orestis liberi sedem cepere circa Lesbum insulam,: circa Mesopotamiam subsistere,: quod circa Syriam nascitur,; Quint. prooem. § 20: initia statim primi libri,; cf. finem,: virentes campos,: cum amor saeviet circa jecur, (cf. : dolor saevit in praecordiis). So esp. freq. in medic. lang.: circa faciem, nares, aures, labra,; .—So in Livy, with names of places, approaching the more general use of later writers, v.infra, C.: quadriduum circa rupem consumptum,: compositis circa Opuntem rebus,: iisdem diebus circa Chalcidem Thoas... eandem fortunam habuit, Weissenb. ad loc.; cf.: multos circa unam rem ambitus fecerim, Weissenb. ad loc.—
( = circum, II. E.) In respect to persons who surround one (as attendants, friends, adherents, etc.), around, about: multa sibi opus esse, multa canibus (sarcast. for indagatoribus) suis, quos circa se haberet,: ex iis trecentos juvenes inermes circa se habebat,: omnes,; : circa regem erat et Phrygum turba,: e spadonibus, qui circa reginam erant,: omne sed officium circa te semper obibat turba tui sexūs,

: quod omnes circa te similes tui effecisti,.—In the language of the imperial court: circa latus alicujus agere,to wait on, altend,.—Hence also without a verb: circa aliquem, = οἱ περί τινα, the attendants, companions of a person: omnibus vero circa eum gratuito aut levi fenore obstrictis,; ; cf. Drak.—

(Peculiar to the form circa). In time, designating nearness, proximity to a definite point of time, about (first in Livy; cf. circiter): postero die circa eandem horam in eundem locum rex copias admovit,: circa eum mensem,: lucis ortum,: lucem,: mediam noctem,: vernum aequinoctium,: Kalendas et Idus Octobr., ; ; ; ; ; —With definite numbers: septimum diem,: undecimam horam,: lustra decem,; .—With general designations of time: tempora illa,: tempora Peloponnesia,: Murenae Cepionisque conjurationis tempus,: Magni Pompeii aetatem,: mortem,: initia imperii,.—And in the designation of periods of time by persons who belonged to them (cf. ante): circa Demetrium Phalerea,about the time of Demetrius Phalereus, Spald.: Tisiam et Coraca,: Philippum,: Ciceronem,: Attium,.—
In numerical designations, about, nearly, almost (first in Livy for the usual ad or circiter): ea fuere oppida circa septuaginta,: quingentos Romanorum,: decem milia Persarum,: sestertium vicies,: quartum milliarium,: selibram,: singulas heminas,.—
(Also peculiar to the form circa, and only in post-Aug. prose; esp. freq. in Quint., occurring more than seventy times.) Trop. for the designation of an object about which, as if it were a centre, any thing moves, is done, etc., around, about, in, in respect to, etc.; depending upon substt., adjj., or verbs.
Upon substantives: circa eosdem sensus certamen atque aemulatio,: circa S litteram deliciae,: verba dissensio,: memoriam suam vanitas atque jactatio,: hoc opiniones,; Plin 8, 16, 19, § 48: quem pugna est,; : voces inani studio,: et saep rura sermo,: classicum brevis et expeditus labor,: hospitia nullum fastidium,: publica circa bonas artes socordia,: principem novo exemplo, i. e. in principe,.—
Upon adjectives: non circa plurium artium species praestantem, sed in omnibus eminentissimum,: jus nostrum attentior,: studia mentis erectae,: lites raras ridiculi,: praecepta utiles sententiae,; : corporis curam morosior,: victum indifferens,: deos ac religiones neglegentior,: administrationem imperii vacuus,: summa scelera distentum,: adfectationem Germanicae originis ultro ambitiosi,: excessus otiosus,: se animati, —
Upon verbs facetum quoque non tantum circa ridicula opinor consistere, : hoc disputatum est,: priores erratur,: formas litterarum haerere,, cf. ; . res tenues morari, Quint 1, 1, 35: consilium elegendi successoris in duas factiones scindebantur,: Medeam, Thyestem (tragoedias) tempus consumas,: successorem omnia ordinari,: ceremonias, item circa omnium ordinum statum quaedam correxit,.!*? Circa very rarely follows its case: quem circa,; ; ; cf. circum, II. fin.

la:verb:circueo.gloss: to go, travel or march around; to circulate

la:verb:circumflecto.html:
circum-flecto, xi, xum, 3, v. a.,
to bend or turn about (Verg. and post-class. writers); prop. of the charioteer in the circus; hence, transf.' longos cursus,; .—
Trop.: circumflexa saecula,returning upon themselves,: anceps labyrinthus et error circumflexus,full of windings and turnings,.—
In later gram. t. t., to mark with a circumflex, to pronounce as long (in Quint., instead of it, circumducere, q. v.): penultimam,: syllaba circumflexa,; P.; ib. et saep.—Adv.: circum-flexē, with a circumflex: promere ( = pronuntiare) syllabam,: enuntiare syllabam, Porphyr. ad ; .

la:verb:circo.html:
circo, āre, 1, v. a.
circus
. = circumeo.
To go about, traverse: montem, Gromat. Vet. p. 326, 17; v. also circito fin.—
To wander through: TOTAM REGIONEM, Inscr. ap. Hermes, 1, 343.

la:noun:circulus.html:
circŭlus, i, m. (contr. circlus, like vinclum = vinculum, ) [kindred with κίρκος, κύκλος, circinus],
a circular figure, a circle: circulus aut orbis, qui κύκλος Graece dicitur, : muri exterior,: circulus ad speciem caelestis arcūs orbem solis ambiit,.—
Esp.
In astronomy, a circular course, orbit: stellae circulos suos orbesque conficiunt celeritate mirabili,: aequinoctialis, solstitialis, septentrionalis,; : lacteus,the Milky Way,; : signifer,; .—
In geog., a zone or belt of the eartb's surface: plura sunt segmenta mundi, quae nostri circulos appellavere, Graeci parallelos, sqq.—
Trop., of time: mensis artiore praecingitur circulo,. —
Meton.
Any circular body; a ring, necklace, hoop, chain, ; ; ; ; .—
A circle or company for social intercourse (very freq.): in conviviis rodunt, in circulis vellicant,; so with convivia also,; ; ; Domit. Mars. ap. ; ; ; ; : cir culos aliquos et sessiunculas consectarl, per fora et circulos locuti sunt, Tac Agr 43; cf : quemcumque patrem familias arripuissetis ex aliquo circulo,; : de circulo se subducere,to withdraw from the assembly,; 10; cf.: densa circumstantium corona latissimum judicium multiplici circulo ambibat,.

la:verb:circumvenio.html:
circum-vĕnĭo, vēni, ventum, 4, v. a., lit.,
to come around something; hence (the coming being considered as accomplished; cf. advenio and adventus, II.).
Lit.
In gen., to be around (a thing), to encircle, encompass, surround (rare): quibus succensis circumventi flammā exanimantur homines,; cf.: donec ignium jactu circumveniretur,; : illum frequentia ingens circumvenit cum plausu,: Cocytos sinu labens circumvenit atro, * : omnium operum magnitudinem circumveniunt cavernae ingentes,: Rhenus insulas circumveniens,flowing around,: planities locis paulo superioribus circumventa,: rami, quos comprehensos manus possit circumvenire,to grasp,; cf. ; ; : singulas urbes,to go around from one city to another, Dietsch.—Far more freq. (esp. in the histt.),
Specif., to surround in a hostile manner, to encompass, beset, invest: ex itinere nostros latere aperto aggressi circumvenere,: ne per insidias ab eo circumveniretur,: consulem,: aciem. : montem opere,: multos ab tergo,: cuncta moenia exercitu,; cf. : legio circumventa,; cf. , ; : armis regiam,fin.; cf. ; 12, 16: cerva circumventa lupis,: hostili custodiā,.—
Trop.
To encompass, beset, oppress, distress, afflict, overthrow: circumventus morbo, exilio atque inopiā, Enn. ap. ; cf. (Trag. v. 42 Vahl.); prol. alt. 46: quasi committeret contra legem, quo quis judicio circumveniretur,; cf. ; ; : aliquem per arbitrum circumvenire,i. e. to lay hold of,: jam te non Siculi, non aratores circumveniunt,: te a Siciliae civitatibus circumveniri atque opprimi dicis?, § 17: potentis alicujus opibus circumveniri urgerique,: ut neque tenuiores proper humilitatem circumveniantur,; so, falsis criminibus,: omnibus necessitudinibus,; cf. : his difficultatibus,: odio accolarum, simul domesticis discordiis,: securitate pacis et belli malo,: testimonio,: multa senem circumveniunt incommoda, * .—
(Cf. circumeo, II. B.) To circumvent, deceive, cheat, defraud one (syn.: decipio, fraudo, fallo): circumventum esse innocentem pecuniā,: an placeret, fenore circumventa plebs,: ignorantiam alicujus,: aliquem falso testimonio,: non sine calliditate circumventus,; cf. .—
In the jurists, to evade, to violate by evading: leges,; : voluntatem defuncti,: orationem,; .—
To obtain possession of, to grasp: omne stagnum,.

la:verb:circumfero.gloss: to carry, bear or move around or about; carry or move around in a circle
senses: to carry, bear or move around or about; carry or move around in a circle
to publish abroad, proclaim, circulate, divulge, disseminate, report
to purify someone by carrying around him consecrated objects
la:verb:circumfero.html:
circum-fĕro, tŭli, lātum, ferre,
v. a. to bear round, or, in gen., to move or carry

round or about (class. in prose and poetry).

Prop.: age circumfer mulsum,pass around,: satiatis vino ciboque poculum... circumferetur,: circumferri vinum largius jubet,: hisce (poculis) etiam nunc in publico convivio potio circumfertur, Müll.: sanguinem in pateris,; Duker: circa ea omnia templa Philippum infestos circumtulisse ignes,: reliquias cenae,: lyram in conviviis,: codicem,: filium suis manibus,: diuque arma circumferens alia tela clipeo excipiebat, corpore alia vitabat,: ter heros Immanem circumfert tegmine silvam,: pavimenta in expeditionibus,: ubique pellem vituli marini,.—Of books carried about for sale, ; : huc atque huc acies circumtulit,; cf. oculos,to cast around,; ; ; ; ; , ext. 2: vultus,; .—Mid.: sol ut circumferatur,revolve,; cf.: linea circumferens, the circumference, Gromat. circum-sŏno, āre, v. n. and a.
(rare but class.).
Neutr., to sound, resound (with something) on every side, to be filled with any sound: locus, qui circumsonat ululatibus cantuque symphoniae,; ; ; . —
Of the sound itself, to resound: dux theatri sui audiens plausum, in modum planctus, circumsonare,.—
Act.
To surround a thing with a sound, to make something to echo or resound, to fill everywhere with a sound: aures vocibus undique, (cf. , and , personare aurem): clamor hostes circumsonat,: Rutulus murum circumsonat armis,; cf.: quā totum Nereus circumsonat orbem, Haupt (al. circumsonat): me luxuria undique circumsonuit,.—
Pass.: Threicio Scythioque fere circumsonor ore,; : nunc procul a patriā Geticis circumsonor armis,.

Aliquid aliquā re, to bind something with something, to encompass, surround: stirpem salice,: ferrum stuppā, Liv 21, 8, 10: totas (radices) caespite,' Roscius circumligatus angui, * ; . —More generally: globum undis,to surround,: aliquem umbrā,.

Neutr.: in poculis repletis circumfluere quod supersit,flows over all around,; cf. .—
Act.: utrumque latus circumfluit aequoris unda,: Cariam circumfluunt Maeander et Orsinus,; cf.: cum aliae aquae subterfluant terras, aliae circumfluant,; ; : cum (oceanus) omnis terras circumfluat,: Smyrna, quam circumfluit Meles fluvius,; ; .—
Trop.

To be present or exist in rich abundance, to abound, overflow: circumfluentibus undique eloquentiae copiis, * : circumfluentibus quietae felicitatis insignibus,.—Also with acc. pers.: secundis rebus, quae circumfluunt vos, insanire coepistis,.—
Circumfluere aliquā re, like abundare, to overflow with, to have an abundance, to be rich in: omnibus copiis, atque in omnium rerum abundantiā vivere,: circumfluens gloriā,: Catilina circumfluens Arretinorum exercitu,.—Also absol.: circumfluere atque abundare,: insatiabilis avaritiae est, adhuc inplere velle, quod jam circumfluit,.—Of too great copiousness of diction: nec redundans, nec circumfluens oratio,too copious,.

la:verb:circumago.gloss: to drive or turn in a circle; to turn round
senses: to drive or turn in a circle; to turn round
la:verb:circumago.html:
circum-ăgo, ēgi, actum, 3, v. a.
To drive or turn in a circle, turn round (most freq. since the Aug. per.; not in Cic. or Quint.): impera suovetaurilia circumagi,.—And with two acc. (on account of circum): terram fundumque meum suovetaurilia circumagi jussi,: (annus) qui solstitiali circumagitur orbe,: chamaeleonis oculos ipsos circumagi totos tradunt,.—Act. in mid. sense (very rare): Aegeum pelagus summotas terras hinc ad promunturium, quod Sunium vocatur, magno ambitu mollique circumagit,rolls around, surrounds,.—
To drive around, produce by going around: pinctis bobus ... aratro circumagebant sulcum, Müll.—Hence,
T. t., to manumit a slave by turning him round. since the slave, in such a case, was taken by his master with the right hand, and turned around in a circle (cf. vertigo, Casaub. , and Dict. of Antiq.); fig.: qui se illi (philosophiae) subjecit et tradidit, statim circumagitur: hoc enim ipsum philosophiae servire libertas est,.—
Trop.
Of time, with se, or more freq. in pass, to pass away, to be spent (so most freq. in temp. perf. and in Liv.): in ipso conatu rerum circumegit se annus,: sed prius se aestas circumegit, quam, etc.,: prius circumactus est annus, quam, etc.,: circumactis decem et octo mensibus,; ; ; 27, 30, 11; 44, 36, 1; ; and in tmesis: circum tribus actis annis,.—In temp. pres.: annus, qui solstitiali circumagitur orbe,: nobis in apparatu ipso annus circumagitur,.—
Of the vicissitudes of fortune, etc.: cum videamus tot varietates tam volubili orbe circumagi,.—
To turn, turn about, wheel around: equos frenis,; ; ; : collum in aversam se,: corpora,: se ad dissonos clamores,: circumagitur, cum venit, imago (in speculis), (340): circumagente se vento,: aciem,: signa,; ; : ut qui (milites) ultimi stabant... verti tamen et in frontem circumagi possent,: se,to turn about,; : legiones,to lead back,. —Hence, prov.: circumagetur hic orbis,the tide will turn,; cf.' praecipua cenationum rotunda, quae perpetuo diebus ac noctibus vice mundi circumageretur,.—
Esp., to agitate, disturb: verna (mala) stomacho inutilia sunt, alvom, vesicam circumagunt,.—
Trop.: hic paululum circumacta fortuna est,changes, is changed,: sed unā voce, quā Quirites eos pro militibus appellarat, tam facile circumegit et flexit,: quo te circumagas?whither will you now turn?: universum prope humanum genus circumegit in se,brought over to his side,.—
(Acc. to circum, II. C.) To run or drive about, proceed from one place to another: (milites) huc illuc clamoribus hostium circumagi,: nil opus est te Circumagi, i. e. that you wander about with me, * .—
Trop.: non pendere ex alterius vultu ac nutu, nec alieni momentis animi circumagi,: rumoribus vulgi circumagi,, 4; 26, 8, 3.—
Aliquem aliquā re = circumdare, to surround with something: fratrem Saturnum muro,.—Hence, circumactus, a, um, P. a., bent around, curved (perh. only in the two Plin.): in orbem circumactus,; ; : sensim circumactis curvatisque litoribus,.

To draw a line as the circumference of a thing (cf. ), i. e. to define, encompass, enclose, lim it, bound, circumscribe (syn.: definio, describo, termino): nullis ut terminis (orator) circumscribat aut definiat jus suum,; cf.: genus universum brevi circumscribi et definiri potest,: exiguum nobis vitae curriculum natura circumscripsit, immensum gloriae,: quibus regionibus vitae spatium circumscriptum est,: ante enim circumscribitur mente sententia confestimque verba concurrunt,: locum habitandi alicui,: Oceanus undique circumscribit omnes terras et ambit,: uti mihi dicas et quasi circumscribas verbis, quid homo sit,.—
To bring within narrow bounds, i. e. to contract, hem in, circumscribe, to hinder free action, to restrain, confine, limit, etc. (syn.: claudo, includo, coërceo).
Esp., of the restrictions or hinderances imposed by one magistracy or authority upon another: Senatus credo praetorem eum circumscripsisset, (cf. just before: an consules in praetore coërcendo fortes fuissent),; ; ; Auct. ap. : ille se fluvio Rubicone et CC. milibus circumscriptum esse patiatur?: gulam et ventrem,: circumscribere corpus et animo locum laxare,: laudes,.—
In gen.: uno genere genus hoc aratorum,to comprehend in one class, Zumpt: totum Dionysium sex epitomis circumscripsit,abridged,: ut luxuriam vilitate circumscribamus,.—
In later medic. lang. circumscribi = minui, to abate, subside: gravedo circumscribitur,; so —
To encircle or go around by writing = scribendo circumdare, i. e. to deceive, cheat, circumvent, entrap, insnare (syn.: circumvenio, decipio): fallacibus et captiosis interrogationibus circumscripti atque decepti,; ; : non circumscribetur, qui ita se gesserit, ut dicat, etc., will not be deceived, i. e. will commit no error, ; .—
In mercantile lang., to deprive of money, to overreach, defraud: adulescentulos,; ; : ab Roscio HS. Ietc.etc.etc.. circumscriptus,: vectigalia,to embezzle,.—
In law, to defeat the purpose of a law, a will, etc., by a forced or too literal interpretation: legem,: ita circumscripto testamento,; : constitutiones, Lact. de Ira Dei, 8.—
Of circumlocution, to involve in language: oratio rem simplicem circumscribens elocutione,; cf.: facetis jocis sacrilegium circumscribens,covering,.—
To cancel; to declare invalid, to annul, invalidate, void, set aside (cf. circumduco, II. D.): hoc omni tempore Sullano ex accusatione circumscripto, (sublato, circumducto, praetermisso, Ascon.): circumscriptis igitur iis seutentiis, quas posui, etc.,.—Hence, circumscriptus, a, um, P. a.
(Acc. to II. A.) In rhet., rounded into periods, periodic: circumscripti verborum ambitus,; cf. ; , and v. circumscriptio.—Adv.: circum-scriptē, in periods: circumscripte numeroseque dicere,: circumscripte complecti singulas res. .—
(Acc. to II. B.) Restricted, limited: brevis et circumscripta quaedam explicatio,: (vis orationis) pressior et circumscriptior et adductior,.—Adv.: circum-scriptē, summarily: circumscripte et breviter ostendere,; . —Sup. of the adj., and comp. and sup. of the adv. not in use.
